_comment: Hand-written stand-in for the Video-MME 'short' video. Replace it with a real recording: `uv run pytest -m live --record tests/e2e/test_step03_overview.py`.
summary: An animated explainer of how mRNA vaccines work. It shows a virus attaching its spikes to a host cell, then explains how an mRNA vaccine teaches cells to make the spike protein so the immune system learns to recognise it.

subjects.name: Virus
subjects.description: A coronavirus particle with spike proteins.

subjects.name: Host cell
subjects.description: A human cell, drawn with a red membrane once the virus invades it.

subjects.name: mRNA vaccine
subjects.description: The vaccine that carries mRNA instructions for the spike protein.

chapters.title: How a virus infects a cell
chapters.summary: The virus attaches its spikes to a host cell and takes it over.

chapters.title: What an mRNA vaccine delivers
chapters.summary: The vaccine's mRNA tells cells to make harmless spike proteins.

chapters.title: The immune response
chapters.summary: The immune system learns the spike and is ready for the real virus.
